mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher policy rates and accelerating inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% signals a collapse in household demand, which reduces consumption and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both fall by >2% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% per month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and supports corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which depresses corporate profit expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of coordinated monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes during non-easing regimes.
